findings.title: Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name
findings.body: Unlike `website`, `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. For anonymous views of restricted TL0 users, `website` is omitted but the new field still exposes its host and, for matching domains, its path. The template also displays this value even when `website` is absent. Gate the derived field with the same restriction. The added `include_website_name` method lacks the required `?` suffix and is not a serializer inclusion hook.

findings.title: Keep the website label synchronized after preference edits
findings.body: `website_name` is now a plain server-provided value rather than a computed property observing `model.website`. However, `User.save()` submits website changes and only applies `bio_excerpt` from the response; it never refreshes `website_name`. Until user details are reloaded, adding a website can leave it invisible, changing one can display the old site's label with the new href, and removing one can leave the old label visible. Update the derived value when saving or retain a reactive calculation.

findings.title: Compare hostnames case-insensitively
findings.body: Ruby's `URI(...).host` preserves hostname case, but the equality and suffix comparisons here are case-sensitive. For an instance at `example.com`, a valid website such as `https://EXAMPLE.COM/user` therefore displays only `EXAMPLE.COM`, despite referring to the same domain. Normalize both hostnames for comparison so these URLs receive the complete path too.
